name: finch-skin-studio
description: Design Finch skins and Home backgrounds: pick a background image and tiling, save AI-designed or current color schemes as custom skins, and switch between built-in and custom skins from a card gallery.

scripts.build: esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --target=node20 --outfile=dist/index.js && cp src/panel.html dist/panel.html && cp src/panel.js dist/panel.js
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx @finchtoys/minitools doctor .

finch.name: Skin Studio
finch.description: Set the Home background image and tiling, save AI-designed or current color schemes as custom skins, and switch skins from a card gallery.
finch.systemPrompt:
Skin Studio manages Finch's visual appearance.
Use skin_studio_theme to design/apply/save/remove color skins:
- action=list: list built-in presets and the user's saved custom skins.
- action=apply: apply a skin. Pass id to apply a built-in preset or a saved custom skin. To design and apply a brand-new AI-generated skin in one step, omit id and pass name+base+colors instead (colors is a partial AppearanceCustomTheme color map: bgRoot,bgMain,bgSidebar,bgElevated,bgHover,bgActive,textPrimary,textSecondary,textTertiary,accent,accentDim,border); add save:true to also persist it into the user's custom skin library in the same call. To switch back to Finch's own built-in theme instead of a custom color skin, pass systemTheme ('system'|'light'|'dark') and omit id/name/colors.
- action=save: persist a skin into the custom library. Pass name+base+colors to save a specific AI-designed palette, or omit colors to save the most recently applied skin ("extract current skin") under a new name.
- action=remove: delete a custom skin by id (built-in presets cannot be removed).
Use skin_studio_background to change the Home background:
- action=set: requires an absolute local image path (imagePath), optional placement ('fill'|'tile', default 'fill') and tone ('brightest'|'bright'|'balanced'|'dark'|'darkest').
- action=clear: remove the Home background and revert to the plain theme surface.
Both tools take effect immediately, exactly like the user editing Appearance Settings themselves. The user can also open the Skin Studio panel (palette icon in the Composer toolbar, or the right Panel launcher) to browse skins as cards, switch back to Finch's own system light/dark/auto theme, manage the background (including choosing a file via the OS's native picker or dragging one in), and export/import custom skins as JSON files — all without going through the AI.
